key_headlines.title: AI Investment Boom Overshadows Middle East War Impact, WTO Doubles Trade Growth Forecast
key_headlines.summary: The WTO has more than doubled its global merchandise trade growth forecast for 2026 as artificial intelligence investment booms offset energy and logistics disruptions from Middle East conflicts. Global trade is expected to grow significantly faster than previously anticipated.

key_headlines.title: Semiconductor Material Shortage Intensifies as AI Chip Demand Surges
key_headlines.summary: Supply shortages are spreading across the semiconductor ecosystem as AI chip demand explodes, with material prices rising sharply. Substrate glass material leader Nitto Denko faces supply pressures despite simultaneous capacity expansions in Japan and Taiwan, with prices rising 30 percent in Q3 alone.

key_headlines.title: US Fiscal Deficit Approaches 2 Trillion Dollars as Interest Payments Soar
key_headlines.summary: The US fiscal deficit is projected to reach nearly 2 trillion dollars in 2026, the largest since 2021, with the deficit-to-GDP ratio expected to exceed 6 percent. Rising interest payments on national debt and lower-than-expected tariff revenues are major contributing factors.

key_headlines.title: OpenAI Revenue Significantly Lower Than Previously Reported
key_headlines.summary: OpenAI's annualized revenue is approximately 50 billion dollars as of September, nearly 200 billion dollars lower than previously disclosed figures, raising fresh concerns about AI sector valuations and bubbles.

key_headlines.title: Trump Delays Military Action Against Iran as Oil Prices Surge 4 Percent
key_headlines.summary: President Trump announced plans to delay military operations against Iran until after midterm elections, citing productive diplomatic discussions. Despite this, crude oil prices jumped 4 percent due to ongoing concerns about Hormuz Strait security and production disruptions.

sections.Hot Economy News: Artificial intelligence investment momentum is dominating global economic headlines, overshadowing disruptions from Middle East tensions. The WTO has more than doubled its 2026 merchandise trade growth forecast, reflecting strong AI-driven demand offsetting energy and logistics challenges. Semiconductor material shortages are intensifying as AI chip demand explodes, with prices rising 30 percent in the third quarter alone, spreading supply constraints across the entire chip ecosystem. Additionally, security concerns have emerged with over 650 hacking attempts against South Korea's national finance system recorded in the first seven months of 2026.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The United States faces mounting fiscal pressures with its deficit approaching 2 trillion dollars in 2026, the largest since 2021, representing a 12 percent increase year-over-year. The deficit-to-GDP ratio is expected to exceed 6 percent, up from 5.8 percent in 2025, rendering the fiscal situation described as unsustainable by policy experts. Interest payments alone account for approximately 1.1 trillion dollars, while tariff revenues fall short of expectations despite the Trump administration's protectionist stance. The combination of lower tariff collections, rising interest costs on national debt, and continued government spending creates a challenging budgetary environment that may require difficult policy choices.
sections.Financial Markets: US Treasury yields have surged above 5 percent, reaching levels not seen in 26 years, with some analysts warning of potential 6 percent yields amid sustained selling pressure. Despite elevated bond yields offering attractive income returns, investors continue deploying capital across both equities and fixed income instruments, suggesting a flight-to-quality dynamic. The South Korean KOSPI index declined 2.62 percent despite strong corporate earnings, reflecting broader market uncertainty stemming from upcoming Federal Reserve policy decisions and US midterm elections on November 3rd. Hedgefund redemptions and market positioning concerns are amplifying interest rate volatility, while uncertainty about additional Fed rate hikes within 2026 continues to weigh on equity valuations globally.
sections.Industry & Technology: The secondary battery sector is experiencing strong recovery with LG Energy Solution reporting record quarterly earnings and increased operating profits of 756 billion won as electric vehicle demand rebounds. Global EV market recovery, combined with expanded US energy storage system production in the second half of 2026, is expected to drive continued performance improvements across major battery manufacturers. Korea, Japan, and 15 EU nations are coordinating joint responses to structural overproduction in five key sectors including electric vehicles, recognizing price-based competition from Chinese manufacturers. Hyundai Motor has surpassed 500,000 cumulative electric vehicle sales in Europe, marking a decade of presence in the market since introducing the IONIQ EV in 2016.
sections.Real Estate: Real estate market dynamics remain complex despite government rhetoric about market flattening, with five key variables including mortgage rates, tax policy uncertainty, and sustained high interest rates significantly influencing property valuations. Young adults in their 20s and 30s are increasingly withdrawing from housing lottery systems due to affordability concerns, as average apartment prices in Seoul reach 1.59 billion won for 59 square-meter units while mortgage lending limits remain constrained. Long-term high interest rates, particularly with mortgage rates exceeding 5 percent, are dampening housing demand and creating headwinds for the residential real estate market. Approximately 1,829 residential units across eight locations nationwide, concentrated in Gyeonggi Province, are scheduled for subscription next week.
sections.International Economy: The US Federal Reserve's recent interest rate increase and signaling of at least one more rate hike within 2026 is generating significant policy uncertainty, with President Trump continuing to pressure the central bank for rate cuts despite inflation concerns. Trump has announced plans to resubmit his nomination for Lisa Cook's removal as a Federal Reserve governor, despite her reconfirmation, raising fresh questions about Federal Reserve independence. Trump's tariff policies are delivering inflationary impacts opposite to his stated intentions, with consumer goods prices rising 2.9 percentage points higher than they would have been without tariffs, according to the New York Federal Reserve. Interest payment burdens are mounting for US households, with monthly interest costs reaching 1.9 million won on a 300 million won loan, creating significant affordability pressures.
sections.AI & Economy: OpenAI's annualized revenue has been disclosed at approximately 50 billion dollars as of September, substantially lower than the previously reported 70 billion dollars figure, raising concerns about valuation accuracy in the AI sector. The discrepancy appears to stem from investor comparisons with competitor Anthropic, where different calculation methodologies led to inflated expectations about OpenAI's revenue trajectory and enterprise value. Nobel Prize-winning economist Paul Krugman has warned that the AI investment boom is crowding out capital from other productive sectors, with technology investment increasing more than 1 percent of GDP while other industries have contracted by over 0.8 percent of GDP. Noomz AI, a startup focused on AI-driven business decision-making using structured data rather than language models, has raised 400 million won in seed funding just seven months after establishment, demonstrating investor appetite for practical AI applications.
sections.Others: South Korea's National Tax Service has identified over 650 hacking attempts against the nation's financial system during the first seven months of 2026, representing 79 percent of the previous year's annual total, though officials report no actual damage has occurred. The government is pursuing establishment of a Korean sovereign wealth fund modeled on Singapore's Temasek, with plans to allow external borrowing by transferring state-owned shares in institutions like Korea Development Bank to the Korea Investment Corporation. Tax collection efficiency concerns persist with reports indicating the Finance Ministry has rejected approximately 80 percent of the National Tax Service's proposed tax law amendments over the past three years, with some proposals being resubmitted multiple times. Maritime fraud issues, including flag of convenience registries enabling tax evasion and exploitative labor practices, continue to plague shipping sectors with weak regulatory oversight compared to developed maritime nations.
